Subject: Request: subprocessor custody, KMS access, SLA & CAIQ follow-up

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking the time on the call yesterday. As we proceed with our vendor review for inference components, our security and procurement teams need a short evidence package so we can finish the risk acceptance:

- Current subprocessor roster (CSV preferred) with country of processing and whether they have any KMS access to customer keys.
- For each infra subprocessor (GPU/compute, storage, logging), a one-line description of custody and whether they can access plaintext data or only encrypted blobs.
- Copy or secure link to your latest SOC 2 report (redacted ok) and the CAIQ/SSP answers you maintain.
- Any SLA/incident notification windows for data access incidents and the escalation contact for security incidents.

If possible, we'd like this by EOD Friday our time (2026-09-10). Let us know if you need to route the SOC 2 link via an NDA or secure upload.

Appreciate it — happy to clarify scope if anything above is unclear.

Best,
Sarah

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:18:03 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: subprocessor custody, KMS access, SLA & CAIQ follow-up

Thanks for the ping. I ran a quick pass and updated the roster: see subprocessors_roster_v2.csv attached. Key notes:

- CloudGPUOps (us-west-1): KMS_access = \"no\" for plaintext customer keys when CMEK is enabled; if customer does not supply CMEK, Redwood-managed key used and CloudGPUOps has encrypted access only — they do not hold plaintext in persistent storage. Custody: ephemeral inference memory only, flushed from node after session.
- StorageLayerCo (eu-central): KMS_access = \"yes\" for metadata encryption keys used for object storage; they cannot decrypt application-layer payloads without Redwood service credentials. Residency: EU.
- LoggingPipeline (global): KMS_access = \"no\" to customer keys; logs forwarded as encrypted blobs; we control decryption within our logging service.

Ben: on SLAs — we can commit to initial incident notification within 1 hour for confirmed data exposure events and a 72-hour preliminary RCA. For contract language, recommend: \"Redwood will notify the customer within one (1) hour of confirming a security incident materially affecting customer data; an initial investigation report will be provided within seventy-two (72) hours.\"

I attached the CSV and marked the CMEK column. I also added a short custody description per provider.

Attachments: [attachment: subprocessors_roster_v2.csv (CSV)]

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Infrastructure Security Lead
Redwood Inference
